correctness.rationale: The convex spectral norm reduces global optimization to invariant kernels. Direct orthogonal decomposition gives all eigenvalues. A negative-square characteristic identity forces the first-regime sharp bound and hub probabilities; a leaf-difference eigenmode and a strict concavity argument prove the second regime. Explicit feasible matrices attain both bounds, with exact equality/uniqueness arguments for invariant hub probabilities. Five exact symbolic identities, 121 full-matrix spectra and 2700 random competitors supplement rather than replace the proof.

value.rationale: The natural pineapple graph has a genuine design regime switch at r=a, where increasing pendant load eliminates the benefit of available clique connections for spectral mixing. Both branches provide exact deployable probabilities and reveal when a star-supported kernel is optimal despite the dense clique. This is a parameter-complete, structurally motivated classification rather than a point computation or substitution.
